question: Which of the following river flows through the Dadra and Nagar Haveli?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dawan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dawan River flows through the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in India.
 
• The river is significant for the region's irrigation and water supply needs.
 
• The Dawan River contributes to the local ecosystem and supports various forms of aquatic life.
 
• The river's catchment area is crucial for the agricultural activities in Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli:**

 
 
• Dadra and Nagar Haveli is a Union Territory in western India.
 
• It is known for its lush greenery, rich tribal culture, and scenic landscapes.
 
• The territory is bordered by the states of Gujarat and Maharashtra.
 
• The economy of Dadra and Nagar Haveli is primarily based on agriculture, forestry, and industrial activities.
 
 
 
• **Tapti River:**
 
 
• The Tapti River, also known as Tapi, is one of the major rivers of peninsular India.
 
• It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The river is 724 km long and drains into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It is significant for the regions it flows through, providing water for irrigation and supporting various ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River:**
 
 
• The Godavari River is the second-longest river in India, after the Ganges.
 
• It originates in the state of Maharashtra and flows through several states, including Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.
 
• The river is known as the "Dakshina Ganga" or "Ganges of the South."
 
• It is crucial for agriculture, providing irrigation to a vast area of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Mithi River:**
 
 
• The Mithi River is a river in the city of Mumbai, India.
 
• It originates from the overflow of the Vihar and Powai lakes and drains into the Arabian Sea at Mahim Creek.
 
• The river is heavily polluted due to industrial waste and sewage.
 
• Efforts are being made to clean and rejuvenate the river to restore its ecological balance.
